messages:
maya: Heads up — saw a sharp 99th-token latency spike for cross-region requests starting 03/17 ~02:10UTC. p99 went from ~60ms -> ~350ms for a subset of routes. Traces suggest a combo of kernel fallback + KV miss amplification.

tom: yikes. which routes/models are hit? repro steps?

maya: affected routes: /v1/generate (route_id=generate-v2) and /v1/chat (route_id=chat-stream). model variant redwood-7b-q4 routed from eu-west -> us-central. Flaky repro but captured several traces. Key symptom: enqueue_ms + kernel_exec_ms are the bulk. KV cache miss ratio jumped ~20% -> ~60% on those traces.

liam: did the kernel selector pick a slower path or involve extra memcpy? any kernel names in the logs?

maya: yes — selector fell back to "matmul-slabs-fp32" instead of the quant-optimized path. Trace shows slab_alloc -> remap -> kernel_launch and a long wait in slab_alloc. There's also larger than usual batch sizes coming from cross-region coalescing.

ana: (quick note) batching heuristics were adjusted last week: max_batch=128 for cross-region to reduce RPCs. That helps throughput but can increase enqueue latency when arrival rates are bursty across zones.

tom: understood. we should split out token-level timing in metrics: enqueue, kv_lookup, kernel_exec, network_rtt, postproc. Also tag by kernel_name and batch_size.

maya: agreed. proposed metric set: inference.token_latency_ms (labels: route, model, kernel_name, region_src, region_dst, token_pos), inference.kv_lookup_ms, inference.kernel_exec_ms, inference.enqueue_ms, inference.batch_size. Buckets: [0.5,2,5,10,20,50,100,200,500]. Also emit routing_decision_reason label with values capacity|latency|price|pin.

infra-bot: [alert] Canary routing policy rollout (2026-03-16T22:05UTC) triggered automatic fallback in 4% of requests for generate-v2 in eu-west -> us-central.

liam: I'll add instrumentation. sending a small example for counters/histogram emission:

```
metrics.histogram("inference.kernel_exec_ms", value, {route: route_id, model: model_name, kernel_name: kernel, region_src: src, region_dst: dst, token_pos: pos})
metrics.counter("inference.kv_miss_total", {route: route_id, model: model_name, region_src: src, region_dst: dst})
```

ana: alert idea (PromQL):

increase(inference.kv_miss_total{route="generate-v2"}[5m]) / increase(inference.request_total{route="generate-v2"}[5m]) > 0.1

maya: dashboard panels I want: 1) stacked token latency by slab (enqueue/kv/kernel/net/post) per-route p50/p95/p99, 2) region->region RTT heatmap median/p95, 3) routing_decision_reason counts + failover rate, 4) kernel_selection waterfall (counts by kernel + avg latency), 5) KV cache miss spike chart + alert.

tom: can we also capture "prior_route" and "chosen_route" when fallback happens so we can compute failover rates by pair? need heatmap of failovers.

maya: yes, emit an event on fallback with prior_route, chosen_route, reason, timestamp. good for dashboards and incident debugging.

liam: implementation plan: PR1 (infra) add histograms/counters + labels; PR2 add event for routing fallback; PR3 dashboard + alerts. I can do PR1 today morning.

ana: for canary we should revert the cross-region max_batch=128 -> 64 to reduce enqueue tail while we investigate.

deploy-bot: canary rollback executed 2026-03-17T02:30:00Z by automated policy (reason: routing-fallback-rate>threshold).

maya: thanks team. Action items recap: liam = metrics + event PR, tom = dashboard skeleton + alert defs, ana = revert canary batch config, maya = run slab profiler & paste trace links. Sync 30m to finalize. :thumbsup:
